A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same GenEx research work, with 14 readable pages including the complete appendix. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the methods, equations, figures, tables and references.

before.justification: v1 reports original loop-consistency experiments in Section 5.2 and evaluations of human and LLM decision making with imagination-augmented policies in Section 5.6, Tables 2–3.

after.justification: v4 retains the original loop-consistency experiments and human/LLM policy evaluations in Section 5 and Tables 2–3.

M1.justification: World initialization, panoramic video transitions, spherical-consistency learning and single-/multi-agent policies remain unchanged in Sections 2–4 and Algorithms 1–2.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same Unreal Engine/Unity environments, controlled Genex-EQA scenarios, single-/multi-agent evaluations and generation, navigation and mapping demonstrations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical: the cubemap baseline and GenEx without SCL in Table 1; random, human, Gemini-1.5 and GPT-4o conditions in Tables 2–3; and TripoSR, SV3d and Stable Zero123 in Figure 11.

E3.justification: Reported metrics and evaluation procedures are unchanged, including averaging over 1,000 closed loops with varying rotations/distances, discarding blocked paths, and using controlled counterparts for Genex-EQA scenarios.

E4.justification: The SCL ablation in Table 1, distance/rotation sensitivity analysis in Figure 9 and single-/multi-agent case studies in Figure 8 are unchanged. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both retain the same loop-averaging description and confidence-score columns in Tables 2–3. Neither adds seed information, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported numerical and qualitative results are retained. For example, GenEx FVD remains 69.5 in Table 1, and GenEx-assisted accuracies remain 85.22% and 94.87% in Tables 2 and 3, respectively.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 changes x to x0 in the initialization factor, making the already-defined initial panorama explicit. This is a notation correction without changed mathematical substance; Appendix Definitions D.1–D.4 and Equations (1)–(4) are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about single-image explorable worlds, 3D consistency, active mapping and imagination-assisted embodied decision making.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning spherical consistency, misleading visual inputs and enhanced human reasoning are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning simulation-to-reality transfer, sensors, dynamic conditions and ethical safeguards.

D1.justification: Figure 1's visible genex.world link targets generative-world-explorer.github.io in v1 and genex.world in v4. This updates access information without establishing changed resource availability. Technical implementation disclosures are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and Section 6's positioning relative to the authors' earlier work, WorldLabs and DeepMind are unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 corrects 'Singel' to 'Single' in Figure 1, lightly edits Figure 13's caption, tidies initialization notation and punctuation, and updates version/date text. The narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1's input label and Figure 13's caption receive small corrections, with minor local typesetting changes. The illustrations, table structures and figure/table placements are otherwise unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 makes small spelling, notation and caption corrections and retargets the project hyperlink. These provide modest editorial maintenance, while the methods, empirical evidence, interpretations and technical disclosures remain substantively identical. They do not establish a meaningful overall quality improvement.
